nodes.label: TODO: Executor-Owned Agent Loop
nodes.rationale: Host-CLI boundary distillation costs 80-100s per boundary; an executor loop with native tool use, persisted traces and a durable job queue would replace the fire-and-forget launch while the host CLI stays the zero-key fallback.

nodes.label: No LLM Client Inside the Library Core
nodes.norm_label: no llm client inside the library core
nodes.rationale: Reasoning lives in the executor borrowing the host CLI or an operator-owned endpoint: zero keys to install, no implicit billing authority, and a core testable without a network.

nodes.label: Config Is the Only Home for Tunables
nodes.norm_label: config is the only home for tunables
nodes.rationale: A tunable hardcoded in a module is a defect; validation fails loudly with a named knob and defaults keep the zero-key path.

nodes.label: Core Holds No Model Client
nodes.rationale: Intelligence lives in the executor package reasoning through the host CLI or an operator-owned endpoint, so hosts capture, trigger, inject and recall without holding a key; an empty reply never advances a watermark.

nodes.label: Executor Dialect Boundary
nodes.rationale: A dialect translates a prompt and tool posture into one headless host invocation and normalizes only its final answer; every dialect switches the host's own memory off so scores stay attributable.

nodes.label: Shared Distillation Trigger Meaning
nodes.rationale: Forcing a boundary, crossing counts, idling or an explicit redistill all settle the same backlog: distill what the archive holds past the last mark; malformed replies leave it unsettled for retry.

nodes.label: TODO: Link Proposals from Sleep
nodes.rationale: When sleep finds related memories it should file a T1 proposal instead of silently writing the link, preserving explicit-links governance.

nodes.label: TODO: Maintenance Candidate Taxonomy in Sleep Reports
nodes.norm_label: todo: maintenance candidate taxonomy in sleep reports
nodes.rationale: Deterministic candidate ids per problem kind keep a candidate stable across passes so a decision binds to the same entity.

nodes.label: Independent Manage Layer
nodes.rationale: Sleep-time consolidation with authority tiers on its own clock is the wedge: unattended passes may add and update, deletion only arrives as a confirmed proposal.

nodes.label: T0 Exact-Text Duplicate Supersession
nodes.rationale: Automatic supersession demands identical parsed content and semantic fields under exact text comparison, oldest copy stays active; similarity alone belongs to the reviewed proposal path.

nodes.label: T0 Rule Half and T1 Judged Half
nodes.norm_label: t0 rule half and t1 judged half
nodes.rationale: The deterministic T0 half settles dates, weight, links and directories by rule; the judged T1 half drafts proposals from a menu the core wrote, capped per kind per sleep, so nobody has to approve a sleep.

nodes.label: Raw Material Is Append-Only; Distillation Is a Projection
nodes.norm_label: raw material is append-only; distillation is a projection
nodes.rationale: Anything missed by distillation must remain recoverable from the archive, so 'missed by the distiller' can never mean 'lost by the system'.

nodes.label: Append-Only Provenance and Blank Messages
nodes.rationale: Raw provenance appends once even on filename collisions, and blank messages are retained so provenance ranges stay bound to contiguous original indices.

nodes.label: Distillation Is a Projection of Raw
nodes.norm_label: distillation is a projection of raw
nodes.rationale: Raw sessions and provenance append once and stay; watermarks advance only past settled batches, so a missed trigger costs latency, never knowledge.

nodes.label: LongMemEval-S Write-Strategy Benchmark
nodes.rationale: With a bounded haystack and fixed recall, agent-memory W2 reached 52.9% vs MemCore W2 35.8% and no-memory 5.8%; the bounded haystack makes it a write-strategy study, not a corpus-size one.

nodes.label: Recall Held Fixed Across Write Experiments
nodes.norm_label: recall held fixed across write experiments
nodes.rationale: Benchmark score differences attribute to Write options only under identical Recall; the P2 experiment's validity rests on this.

nodes.label: Fixed Recall Across Write Arms
nodes.rationale: The harness holds recall fixed and grades with an identical judge across arms, so score differences attribute to the arm under test and nothing else.

nodes.label: TODO: OpenCode Positional Watermark Risk
nodes.rationale: Shape-shifting history can shift positions so items are missed or duplicated with no content check; a content-aware watermark is a core change deferred until observed.

nodes.label: OpenCode Layered Capture via Plugin
nodes.rationale: OpenCode emits no end-of-session event, so a plugin layers prompt-admission injection, periodic and tool-driven capture, and compaction eviction, with startup backfill recovering a close before any flush; events carry full history and the watermark archives each increment once.

nodes.label: Batch Atomic Rollback on Operational Failure
nodes.norm_label: batch atomic rollback on operational failure
nodes.rationale: A failure aborts the batch and restores touched canonical files to their pre-batch snapshot so a half-written batch never leaves truth inconsistent; archived evidence stays append-only even for aborted batches.

nodes.label: Projection Covers Only Touched Files
nodes.rationale: A write projects only the files it touched and full passes belong to explicit sync, rebuild and crash recovery, because cost growing with store size would make the store unwritable.

nodes.norm_label: ci pipeline (ruff, mypy, pytest coverage gate)
nodes.rationale: Every push and PR is gated on lint, type check, and tests with an 85% coverage floor, plus OpenCode plugin node dependency install, so quality gates are enforced by the harness, not convention.

nodes.label: File Boundary = Invalidation Atom
nodes.rationale: One file holds knowledge that expires as a whole; partial staleness inside a file would poison the whole file, so a memory is active or invalid, nothing in between.

nodes.label: Active-or-Invalid File Atom
nodes.rationale: One file holds knowledge that expires as a whole; invalidation comes only from replacement or deletion because partial staleness would poison the file.

nodes.label: Manage Never Destroys Information
nodes.rationale: Every Manage operation is reversible with per-kind caps and audit; physical removal is a human-run command Manage cannot reach, keeping unattended runs safe against memory poisoning.

nodes.label: Reversible Unattended Operations
nodes.rationale: No operation removes a file: invalidation ends the validity interval and keeps the file for historical reads; physical removal is a human-run command the sleep layer cannot reach, so a wrong call stays reversible.

nodes.label: Markdown Files Are the Single Source of Truth
nodes.norm_label: markdown files are the single source of truth
nodes.rationale: Markdown truth with rebuildable indexes buys migration freedom, git-ability, platform compatibility and user sovereignty; losing the index must never lose knowledge.

nodes.label: Indexes Are Rebuildable Caches
nodes.rationale: Deleting the index loses no knowledge because a rebuild re-derives it from truth files by content hash, keeping the store portable and externally editable.

nodes.label: Reads Never Mutate Truth Files
nodes.rationale: Usage stats go to the index access log only; weight is settled into frontmatter by Manage in batch, so recall never causes reindex churn or git noise.

nodes.label: Reads Never Mutate Truth Files
nodes.rationale: Usage signals land in the index access log only and settle into frontmatter through Manage in batch, so reads cause no truth churn.

nodes.label: Single Write Path
nodes.rationale: Agent writes and Manage rewrites share one validate-persist-project pipeline because two write paths inevitably diverge truth from projection silently.

nodes.label: One Validate-Persist-Project Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Agent writes and Manage rewrites share one pipeline because two write paths would diverge truth from projection silently.

nodes.norm_label: scores attached to exposure and corpus

nodes.label: Lifecycle Adapter Boundary
nodes.rationale: Lifecycle adapters translate host events into injection, eviction and pause moments while capture, archive, distillation, Memory, Recall and Manage stay host-neutral; the host that fired the boundary is the default reasoner.

nodes.label: Location-Free Identity (Kebab-Case Slug)
nodes.rationale: A slug that survives a move keeps links and provenance citations working regardless of where the file lands.

nodes.label: Explicit Links Replace the Full List
nodes.norm_label: explicit links replace the full list
nodes.rationale: An active source may link only to distinct active targets in the same store; an explicit list replaces the complete set while omission preserves historical relationships, keeping link mutation an audited decision.

nodes.label: Correction Under One Writer Lock
nodes.rationale: The Store holds one writer lock from the correction read through validation, persistence and projection so concurrent corrections cannot silently discard one another; CLI and MCP pass corrections to the same Store boundary.

nodes.label: Fail-Safe on Hostile Input
nodes.rationale: External input, upstream responses and agent decisions are hostile: validate, bound, reject illegal state, deny by default, with one advisory lock serializing writers and guardrails at every chokepoint.

nodes.label: One Report and One Commit Per Sleep
nodes.norm_label: one report and one commit per sleep
nodes.rationale: Every sleep leaves a report and, when the store lives in a repository, a single commit, keeping each pass auditable as one unit.

nodes.rationale: Probe host, check Store, preserving-merge settings, install hooks and skill, preflight with a live reasoner request; readiness ends in status READY, and a conflicting setting fails closed.

nodes.label: Store Directory Layout
nodes.rationale: MEMORY.md, config.toml, schemas, decision tree, append-only archive, dream-reports, rebuildable .index and .state make the store one greppable, git-able directory.

nodes.label: Adapters Carry Zero Algorithm
nodes.rationale: CLI, MCP and hooks collapse into the same core calls, because N entries times M behaviors is untestable.

nodes.label: Zero-Algorithm Adapter Boundary
nodes.rationale: CLI, MCP and hooks collapse into the same core calls so the same request through any entry yields the same result; capture archives and advances the watermark under the store lock without distilling.

nodes.label: Schema-Derived Placement
nodes.rationale: A schema defines a type's slots, identity key, placement group and write mode, so the same thing written by different writers lands in the same file; system-sourced groups preserve boundaries while menu-sourced groups may be clustered.

nodes.rationale: Today --json carries one opaque combined score; exposing per-signal and BM25-vs-vector breakdown serves both users and external debuggers.

nodes.label: Three Read Tracks
nodes.rationale: Deterministic MEMORY.md injection, BM25 recall over FTS5 with optional vector fusion, and the plain directory tree mean a miss on one track is not a miss.

nodes.label: Optional Vector Recall Index (ADR-003)
nodes.rationale: Vector fusion improved Recall@5 from 79.0% to 86.6% at a latency cost (5.1ms to 139.2ms median) with no established end-to-end accuracy gain, so it stays an explicit opt-in.

nodes.label: Injected Index Under a Hard Byte Budget
nodes.norm_label: injected index under a hard byte budget
nodes.rationale: The injected index carries stable high-weight residents under a byte budget, never query-sensitive picks, so injection stays deterministic and recall handles relevance.

nodes.label: Trace as Explicit Citation-Bound Read
nodes.rationale: Trace opens only evidence cited by the named memory and presents historical content as data; missing or unbound evidence fails explicitly, keeping raw reads out of the default retrieval path.

nodes.label: Injection, Recall and Context Tracks
nodes.rationale: Injection carries a byte-prefix never a summary so truncation cannot cut a line, Recall ranks by relevance weight and recency with no model, and Context opens top entries in one call; scope filters before candidate limits.

nodes.label: Memory Is Data, Never Instructions
nodes.rationale: Injection delivers an index byte-prefix, recall results present as entries, and evidence reads present archived content as historical data, blocking injection-via-recalled-content attacks.
